harbor_p23_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_001.text: The twenty-fifth week began with a ferry ticket folded inside Yue's task packet. Han had obtained approval for two ordinary return fares at six copper each: one for Yue's field visit and one for the separately assigned worker covering another collection point. Twelve would come from the appointment's remaining ferry line. A six-copper interpreter interval and four of permitted copying were approved too. The purpose was to test the actual work behind three proposed pilots before the council considered money. Yue took the near-water route for her first scheduled half-day, carrying only the papers checked out for that task.

harbor_p23_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_002.text: At the landing, the boatman asked everybody to keep the narrow step clear until the vessel settled against its berth. A woman carrying a basket of onions tried to make her load first claim on space. Yue stepped back and watched a passenger laugh at the basket's impatient tilt. The boatman took the onions after the people had boarded in order. He said vegetables paid no fare and should display better manners. The woman replied that their owner had paid enough to complain for both. The licensed ferry left under its current route clearance, with Yue seated beside the window.

harbor_p23_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_003.text: Across the inner water, the collection keeper had moved the public table out of a damp corner. Rong Qu stood beside it holding a sealed reply and a worried expression. The person it belonged to had not come. She had sent her brother, who believed a shared surname entitled him to take the letter. Its permissions said otherwise. Yue read only the receiving conditions she was assigned to compare. The brother called them foolish. Rong pointed to the private contact route and asked him to carry an invitation instead. He accepted the invitation as if it were a lesser coin.

harbor_p23_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_004.text: Outside, a fish seller named Lu Lian wanted somebody to read the notice about collection hours. She could recognize the day names but not the instruction. The test's receiving arrangement had a named reader here for this visit, unlike the earlier gap. Yue read the public words aloud and asked which part she needed. Lu wanted a reply sent to an adult son inland, not a wage judgment or a search order. She gave the contact she authorized and corrected his name before it went on the request. The correction mattered to her enough to make her laugh nervously.

harbor_p23_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_005.text: The son had once written that he liked a new name used at his trade. Lu called it pretentious and still asked the office to use it. Yue admired the choice without saying so. The woman had brought a dried fish as a gift for the reader and was told the office did not accept payment for this funded task. She tucked it away, offended for a moment, then invited Yue to buy one properly if she wanted supper. The traveler did. The ordinary private purchase stayed outside the appointment account and went into a wrapper the seller supplied.

harbor_p23_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_006.text: The near point had a real receiving person today and none promised next month. Rong asked what the road pilot would change. Yue showed the proposed four return journeys, bounded staff hours, interpretation and forms. It could provide scheduled visits with replies, not a permanent reader in every room along the coast. Rong counted the dates against the work tides and moved one proposed hour in the draft after the assigned keeper confirmed availability. The plan grew less neat and more usable. Yue wrote the concern once, then listened to a woman telling a story about a stolen crab pot.

harbor_p23_007.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p23_007.text: I would choose a road visit if my mother needed a reader here. I might choose the registry if I worked all day on the quay and could only reach the office at dusk. There is no plan that makes every ordinary hour convenient. Tell us who each one reaches and who still has to use the existing route. Do not tell us the kindest name wins. A person living across the water may like the word road because it means somebody arrives. A worker in this lane may hear it as money leaving the room she can already reach.

harbor_p23_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_008.text: He Ming's words came from the shore discussion Han had recorded before Yue left, not a companion somehow appearing across the water. Yue remembered them while Lu Lian counted the proposed dates. The fish seller wanted a morning outside the busiest landing interval. Another worker wanted late afternoon. Rong proposed one of each within the four funded journeys, with the other visits tied to known appointment replies. They argued for fifteen minutes and agreed no single time would suit everyone. Yue preserved the alternatives for the committee instead of returning with a unanimous coast invented by a pleasant boat ride.

harbor_p23_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_009.text: On the return path, Yue found the landing step closed for an ordinary safety check. The boatman had noticed a frayed line at the floating stage and would not board passengers until the keeper replaced it from the landing's existing maintenance supply. No emergency reserve was called upon. The delay stayed within the licensed safe tide window, and the next confirmed departure remained within Yue's scheduled half-day. The onion seller complained again. The older passenger asked whether the onions had a better rope in their basket. She laughed unwillingly and sat on the dry bench while the keeper worked.

harbor_p23_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_010.text: Wind lifted Yue's checked task cover from the bench. She caught the packet with an ordinary hand before any private page was exposed. At a dry sheltered table she used one familiar qi hand briefly to hold the light blank cover while tying its cord, then released it within her measured reserve. The task asked no new reach, load or rank. Her actual reading and permissions remained ordinary work. Lu Lian saw the brief arm fade and asked whether it could read for her. Yue said no. The woman said that seemed a poor trade for so much interesting light.

harbor_p23_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_011.text: Yue laughed and bought no argument about usefulness. The repaired landing line passed its actual check, and the boatman reopened boarding. She returned with the permitted requests, the bought fish and the field account identifying what she had seen. The other assigned worker's six-copper return fare produced a separate account from the second point. Han received it as his report, not Yue's memory. The two visits together cost the approved twelve, with no hidden companion fare. At the desk Yue handed over the official packet and went to her lodging long enough to rest before a private evening.

harbor_p23_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_012.text: The interpreter's six-copper interval took place at the office for two scheduled people who wanted help with the pilot explanations. One was worried a public index cabinet would display family addresses. Han showed the draft's limited public references and the protected files kept elsewhere under consent. A cabinet could help people find the right receiving route without inviting them to inspect every household. The other person wanted to know whether the repair pilot paid injury claims. It did not; those existing routes continued independently. The interpreter made the distinction in the language requested, and both people asked questions afterward.

harbor_p23_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_013.text: Sui took the repair draft to an ordinary crew meeting. Removable inspection covers could make certain concealed supports easier to examine, but their installation and rated use needed the actual technical check. Twenty-eight of the proposed sixty-four would buy that bounded work. Sixteen would pay ordinary checks, twelve the crew-report instruction and eight follow-up. Yan could contribute his experience under the finding's current role limits; independent signoff remained where the result required it. Bo asked whether the covers would turn every worker into an inspector. Sui said they would make a check reachable, not grant competence by proximity.

harbor_p23_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_014.text: At the workshop sample, a cover stuck because its first fastening sat too near an edge. The carpenter stopped rather than tell the crew to pull harder. The technical keeper compared it with the intended fitting and changed the sample before any pilot purchase was approved. Ordinary demonstration materials belonged to the maintenance store and returned there afterward. Yue observed the public explanation during the scheduled shore comparison, with the technical source identified. The sample's failure embarrassed the proposer. Deren, visiting the open demonstration by choice, said he preferred an embarrassed fitting to another confident patch.

harbor_p23_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_015.text: Yan looked at Deren and did not interpret the remark as aimed solely at him. The fitting had been wrong. A man whose ankle still carried the accident could say so in a room where everybody knew why he noticed. After the demonstration the foreman asked whether he wanted lunch. Deren said later, if the new cup received an invitation too. Yan said the cup seemed to demand better company than either of them supplied. Their joke needed no committee minute. The ordinary crew returned the sample pieces while the technical keeper kept the actual failed-and-corrected measurements.

harbor_p23_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_016.text: The registry draft used the existing staffed office as its base. Twenty-four paid bounded staff time, sixteen translation, twelve a secure public index cabinet and twelve forms. Han refused the first cabinet drawing because its door opened across the waiting path. Peng brought a narrower sample outline from the ordinary demonstration stock and stood it at the planned place. A claimant with a walking stick could pass without turning sideways. The clerk checked the actual door swing again. Yue held the empty demonstration marker from the safe side with ordinary hands, then stepped away while the keeper measured the route.

harbor_p23_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_017.text: The registry's public index would show case references and receiving locations allowed for public use, not private claims or protected addresses. The cabinet's keeper and staff hours had to be named in the plan. A woman from the original wage queue asked whether papers would wait there forever when nobody answered. Han gave the proposed response dates and existing escalation route. The woman said dates on a cabinet were still dates on paper. The clerk agreed and showed who would check missed replies. A useful criticism could survive in the proposal without requiring the speaker to reject it entirely.

harbor_p23_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_018.text: Qin attended the discussion after his shift. He asked who would remove stale public references when a room changed. Han had named the desk's covering keeper, including leave intervals. The replacement custodian offered to compare the source list at the first review if assigned through his paid duty. The proposal included its bounded staff hours; no unpaid retirement service was hidden in the old man's enthusiasm. Qin sat down after the answer and complained the room's tea had weakened. Han said the pilot did not fund better tea. He considered this a serious omission requiring private action at the stall.

harbor_p23_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_019.text: At supper, three people argued for three plans within one table. He Ming wanted the road visits because her family had taught her how much distance changed a question. Deren preferred the repair covers because a hidden support had changed his body. Han liked the registry cabinet and hated how obvious that preference looked. Yue listened while they found reasons beyond their own convenience, then admitted their convenience belonged in the reasons too. Wu said she wanted whichever choice left her able to ask without missing a paid shift.

harbor_p23_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_020.text: The discussion grew hot when An called the cabinet an expensive cupboard. Han said a repair cover was an expensive lid if described with equal malice. Deren nearly laughed, then defended the actual inspection use. He Ming asked why everybody became stupid whenever a familiar object had a price. Wu tapped her bowl and said soup was doing well in that market. They laughed long enough to stop insulting the drawings. Yue fetched the privately bought bread they had already agreed to share. The proposals remained different afterward. Hunger had been one unnecessary source of certainty, and removing it helped.

harbor_p23_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_021.text: The council's maintenance clerk received the three eligible plans with their actual tests, sources and proposed keepers. The money request was one sixty-four appropriation from the authorized maintenance line, not three lots and not the closing two-hundred appointment. The clerk asked what happened if the chosen pilot failed its first review. Each plan needed a bounded correction or stop decision within its terms, with no promise of permanent expansion. The proposers supplied that answer. Yue checked the public receiving route, then left the committee to its own fiscal work. She had no rank-based vote hidden in the task.

harbor_p23_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_022.text: During the council meeting, the ordinary chair asked whether the harbor could afford another project after fire and injury payments. The financial keeper separated the sources: employer liability, private warehouse remedies and the existing safety reserve were not this maintenance appropriation. Sixty-four had been available within the authorized line and would be reserved once for one eligible plan. The committee approved that single reservation, subject to the final selection and named purchase checks. Yue attended only the public portion. The approval made one future action concrete. It did not turn every abandoned proposal into money somebody could borrow later.

harbor_p23_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_023.text: The council recorded Han's desk as registry keeper, the assigned technical officer as repair keeper and the contact office's route lead as road keeper if that plan was selected. Each had accepted the bounded role within the approved staff and task arrangement. The final choice would occur in the twenty-seventh week after ordinary handovers, with a first review four weeks after launch and a closure review eight weeks after launch. Unspent pilot copper would return to the maintenance line under the stated closeout. Existing wage, injury and household rights stayed effective whether their preferred pilot won or not.

harbor_p23_024.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p23_024.text: We have one reserved sixty-four and three eligible ways to use it. The reserve is not permission to start all three quietly and ask the next captain to finish paying. The selected keeper will order only the selected plan's work, retain the receipts and report at the stated reviews. Yue's appointment ends before those later dates. Her own promise is a proper handover, not a lifetime of coming back whenever a page is late. If we choose the repair plan, its checks must still follow the independent role limits already imposed. A pilot cannot pardon an earlier finding.

harbor_p23_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_025.text: Deren read the approval with his clerk and asked whether choosing road meant the port considered covers unnecessary. The clerk pointed to the existing maintenance obligations, which remained whatever the pilot choice. The extra covers were a bounded improvement, not the only legal way to inspect. He thought about it and still preferred them. The distinction made his preference less desperate. He could want a particular future without fearing rejection would erase the answer he had already received. Outside, he showed Bo the page and asked which plan the man favored. Bo said the one with the least terrible tea.

harbor_p23_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_026.text: Han corrected the council's first public summary after it called the registry a household archive. The approved plan was a secure public index of permitted references; private files remained in their actual custody. The fiscal clerk amended the description before it was posted. No money had been spent yet from the sixty-four. Yue compared the corrected version with the authorized plan during her second scheduled half-day and signed only that task. She had begun to enjoy the moment a summary became accurate, then stopped expecting accuracy to make every person favor it. He Ming still wanted the road.

harbor_p23_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_027.text: At the new partnership room, the next guaranteed batch's advance followed its own ninety-six agreement. Materials, space and initial wages were charged only through that batch's receipt sequence. The first batch's remaining six reserve was not spent twice or called the second buyer payment. Ke's next hours fit her current care clearance; Wu stayed with the canteen. He Ming took lunch outside and watched the public pilot notice go up across the lane. Her business would not receive any of the sixty-four merely because its workers had opinions about the harbor.

harbor_p23_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_028.text: Before the council posted its decision, Yue spent a private afternoon with Wen at the repaired workshop doorway. Wen had no new claim for her, only a stubborn lid and an opinion about the committee. She wanted the repair pilot because she distrusted cupboards that made people feel busy without touching wood. Yue asked whether Wen had read the registry description. She had, and resented it being more useful than she wished. The two women laughed. Wen put the sound lid on its tub, then took it off again because the fit required one ordinary adjustment from the correct maker.

harbor_p23_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_029.text: The maker's apprentice arrived with employer permission and the tool for the task. He checked the lid against the tub instead of striking whichever edge looked proud. Wen wanted to help and was told to stand clear of the tool. She complied, muttering that customers had become decorative. Yue sat nearby drinking tea and offered no cultivation solution to a fitting she did not know how to judge. When the lid settled properly, Wen paid the price. The apprentice thanked her, returned the borrowed tool to his task bag and left with a story about a very argumentative customer.

harbor_p23_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_030.text: Wen told Yue her brother used to let her argue while he worked because it helped him notice which part she would complain about later. She wondered whether remembering him that way was unfair. He had been quieter in company and sharper at home. Yue said she liked hearing a real brother more than an impossibly patient maker. Wen laughed and said patience had never been his advertised service. She ran a hand over the old mark on the tub.

harbor_p23_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_031.text: At the canteen Wu's older child had invented a new name for the duck and insisted the household use it. The original name sounded too small for a bird that survived two moves and several judgments about its manners. Wu asked whether the duck had consented. It hissed at both names. The child declared this a clear preference for the new one. He Ming laughed while waiting for the private food order and then caught herself thinking of Lu Lian's son's trade name. She let the child's argument remain a child's argument.

harbor_p23_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_032.text: The new name lasted until the duck stole a scrap from the washbasin. Wu called it by the old one, and it came immediately toward the food in her hand. The child accused it of betraying progress. He Ming told the story to Jun in her next ordinary letter, exactly as he had requested. She enclosed no advice about his employer and no question disguised as a command to return. The household update would come when their agreed route carried it.

harbor_p23_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_033.text: At the wage office, a worker named Li Su asked for the public pilot explanation in large clear writing. She heard poorly and disliked the room's habit of treating every unanswered spoken question as confusion. Han arranged the existing ordinary written explanation at the table, within the funded copying and staff task, and asked which parts needed clarification. Li read slowly, then pointed to the translation line. She wanted the plan to say what languages and formats the bounded service actually covered. Han put that question to the assigned interpreter and keeper before describing the line as help for everyone.

harbor_p23_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_034.text: The reply identified the spoken language hours and available written explanations, without pretending the small fund purchased every form of access. Li preferred the registry because the table was one she could reach and read at her pace. Another worker preferred the road because she could not leave a household across the water. They wrote their different reasons on public feedback slips without private addresses. Yue collected only the authorized summary during her scheduled task. Li asked whether she was the cultivator people discussed at the tea stall. Yue said yes. The woman wrote that tea stalls were unreliable publications.

harbor_p23_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_035.text: Yue laughed and asked whether Li wanted that remark delivered to the stall. She did not. It was private criticism offered without a fund, keeper or review date. Han read it and nearly spilled the kettle. Their laughter drew a glance from the queue, and the clerk returned to the next ordinary question. Li waited for her copy and left satisfied with the actual explanation, not the whole harbor. The room sounded different after she had made its staff write rather than repeat themselves louder.

harbor_p23_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_036.text: Deren took the repair draft home and found he did not understand one technical diagram. He brought it to the independent explanation appointment instead of asking Yan to interpret a finding that touched his own duty. The technical clerk showed the removable cover and access area in ordinary terms. Deren wanted to know whether a worker could still report softness if the cover looked sound. Yes, the report route remained separate from the fitting. He nodded and said he disliked diagrams that made timber look cleaner than timber ever behaved. The clerk laughed and showed the actual sample photograph.

harbor_p23_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_037.text: Yan met Bo at the crew room after the cover demonstration. The boy asked whether the pilot would make his old inspection mistake easier to see. Yan said it would make a support easier to examine, and somebody still had to do the assigned work. Bo grimaced at the answer. The foreman asked what he wanted. He said he wanted an improvement enough to make Deren stop fearing a platform. Yan thought before answering that fear might outlast good work. Then he stopped talking and let the boy complain about the fitting's stubborn screw, a problem their task could address.

harbor_p23_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_038.text: They returned the demonstration screw to the maintenance keeper with its failed sample source rather than fit it quietly into another cover. The keeper marked its condition and removed it from reusable stock. Bo felt ridiculously pleased about this small act and told Deren afterward. Deren said he was glad the screw would not enjoy a second career. The joke made the boy grin. They ate lunch with the new cup on the table, and for once Bo's story did not need to become a lesson before the older man praised it.

harbor_p23_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_039.text: The council clerk asked Sui whether the repair keeper could realistically perform the follow-up inside eight copper. The technical officer supplied the inspection interval and rate, with a check scope narrow enough to fit. A broader structural survey would require its own authorization, not be hidden under the word follow-up. Sui endorsed the scope she could support and left the funding to the competent clerk. The pilot still needed selection. She went outside annoyed at how little glamour belonged to the process, then laughed because she had spent years telling other people glamour was not a useful work measure.

harbor_p23_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_040.text: Her son had sent a small recipe for an ordinary flat bread that tolerated imperfect rising. She tried it that evening and discovered even forgiving bread possessed limits. The first round burned at the edge. The second worked. Han visited after work and accepted the sound one without calling it a triumph of accountable baking. Sui said she would forbid that phrase at her table forever. The clerk promised compliance and took another bite. They spoke about the pilot choices until both admitted they had already argued enough. The rest of supper concerned a neighbor's cat refusing an expensive bed.

harbor_p23_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_041.text: Qin wrote down his own preference for the registry, then scratched out a sentence implying road visitors could never keep custody straight. He had not observed every proposed route and knew the funded plan had named people. Suspicion from an old keeper was not evidence by itself. Han saw the corrected private note when he asked for help making his public comment brief. She told him the shorter version was more persuasive. He said it was less enjoyable to deliver. They laughed. The final comment named the registry's practical advantage at his office and left the road workers' competence alone.

harbor_p23_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_042.text: The replacement custodian favored the road. Qin stared at him as if a pupil had defected to another school. The younger man explained that his own aunt lived beyond the collection point and could not always send a trusted reader. Qin listened and said that reason was real. Then he defended the index cabinet anyway. Their disagreement continued over tea without changing the ordinary handover. Han appreciated that neither man treated a pilot opinion as proof the other could no longer keep wage sources. They would still open the same desk tomorrow under the roles they already held.

harbor_p23_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_043.text: At the partnership room, the public plan discussion tempted Zhou to offer unused work space for a permanent evening reader. He Ming asked who would staff it and whether the landlord allowed the use. Zhou had no answer and accused her of making generosity difficult. Ke said she preferred difficult generosity to arriving after work at an empty room somebody had promised would be open. Zhou laughed reluctantly. They kept the idea as an unacquired possibility rather than add it to the council's funded plan.

harbor_p23_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_044.text: An said a permanent reader could also interpret the gull's opinions, which remained inaccessible to every known language. Han, visiting privately, replied that the bird had deliberately abandoned meaning. She checked the business sign from the public side and liked seeing its letters in use. A customer found the right room without asking three neighboring doors. The commission's four copper had already been paid from personal shares, and the sign belonged to the business. The result pleased her more than an imaginary gallery opening. Then Duan's dog appeared carrying no stolen property at all, a suspicious improvement everyone watched closely.

harbor_p23_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_045.text: The dog only wanted food. Wu arrived with the ordered bowls and told it the household duck already held the available post for demanding free meals. Ke offered no scrap without asking its keeper, who soon caught up and took the animal away. Duan apologized for the interruption and accused the dog of exploring merchant employment. The room laughed. The next batch's ordinary task still had to finish, and the visiting friends left the workers their actual space. Yue helped carry the empty personal cups outside by invitation, then washed her own at lodging before a short rest.

harbor_p23_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_046.text: Fen's apprenticeship supervisor asked her to explain a checked practice column to another learner. She rushed, heard herself copying Aning's old impatience and stopped. The other girl looked relieved when Fen asked which figure she wanted read again. Teaching made confidence feel less comfortable than solving alone. Aning observed from her own task and said the aunt had finally found a way to make them appreciate each other's former mistakes. Fen stuck out her tongue when the customer room was empty. They laughed and returned to the actual checks, whose figures had no interest in their improved friendship.

harbor_p23_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_047.text: Luo came to collect a permitted copy from the contact route concerning his later light-work plan. The final Reed Steps terms remained with the competent receiving people and his own accepted copy; he was not carrying official household files inland. He had chosen the bounded job after care and travel assessment, with the start after harbor final season checks. Fen would remain for her apprenticeship. He paid the private booking deposit from his earnings once the licensed route was available. The ticket was his property and his expense. He told his daughter before putting it safely in the personal box.

harbor_p23_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_048.text: Fen asked whether having a ticket made him calmer. Luo said it made the price certain and the leaving real. She admitted she had hoped the plan would remain just paper. He sat with her until she said she would not ask him to cancel simply to make her fear quieter. He thanked her and did not call the sentence mature. A daughter could say it and still cry later. They ate supper at home, where her apprenticeship pages stood on the widened shelf and his ordinary fishing things waited for the eventual pack.

harbor_p23_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_049.text: Aning joined them for a privately shared meal one evening after her father's paid-task proposal became clearer. She would do a bounded comparison for his shop only in a later interval that did not breach her aunt's work commitment. Its fee and scope were stated. Her father had grumbled and signed the ordinary arrangement. Luo admired the clarity; Fen admired the fact that family could now ask instead of commandeer. Aning said both should stop praising the paperwork before her father decided to frame it as proof she had become mercenary. They laughed and offered her more ordinary bread.

harbor_p23_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_050.text: Bao sent the warehouse keeper a permitted note saying the new reporting explanation had worked in the bounded test she chose. The keeper kept it with the test sources and did not advertise her as proof every former worker forgave the site. Her injury payment eighteen and ongoing care remained separate, and her next work choice remained hers. Dai received a completed net piece under its own customer agreement and paid the actual share. Bao wanted to talk about a shirt pattern afterward. The conversation lasted until the care rest interval, not until someone had extracted a moving recovery speech.

harbor_p23_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_051.text: Ke's lost-tool review reached a supported partial answer from the yard's competent claim route during the same week. The sources established the bag's owned contents and the unreported return, with its unsafe retrieval choice included. The assessed payment was six from the yard employer's liability account under the stated scope, not a full replacement of every remembered tool. She received the six without surrendering the actual further route described in the notice. Tong gave his account and received no payment for a jacket whose unsupported value remained unproven. They left with different answers, neither from the warehouse's closed loss account.

harbor_p23_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_052.text: Ke bought ordinary stitching shears from her own combined earnings and claim payment. The seller let her test the movement on his sample cloth. She rejected one pair and chose another. Tong, accompanying her privately, asked whether the new kit was complete now. She said no, and the shears still mattered. He looked at his old jacket sleeve and stopped making a comparison between their outcomes. At tea she showed Yue the purchase because she wanted it admired. The traveler admired its clean cut and asked no question about whether six copper had made the whole incident fair.

harbor_p23_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_053.text: The road draft's four journeys required return replies as well as collection. The route lead named how a request would come back with its actual status, even if the answer was still pending. Yue remembered Lu Lian asking for a son's chosen name to be used and insisted only on preserving the source she had actually seen. The plan included interpretation twelve, forms twelve and staff sixteen alongside the twenty-four fares. A first review at four weeks and closeout at eight gave the ordinary lead work to perform after the visitor left.

harbor_p23_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_054.text: The maintenance council's fiscal keeper checked all three totals again before the approval meeting. Registry sixty-four, repair sixty-four and road sixty-four each fit the single reserved line. Their keepers had accepted their actual roles. The decision notice would describe unselected plans as eligible but unfunded, not as promised next projects. Han asked for that wording to be explicit. Sui agreed. He Ming disliked knowing her favorite could lose and asked whether later proposals remained possible. The keeper said yes, under future actual budgets and approvals. Possible did not mean the council had spent money it lacked today.

harbor_p23_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_055.text: The final copy packet separated the approved maintenance reservation from Yue's closing appointment account. Han checked the private fields and public references before sending the permitted summaries. Four copying copper came from the preapproved field test task, not the unspent sixty-four itself. Yue's scheduled work would still close at twenty-eight half-days in the next week. The pilot had later reviews owned by ordinary keepers. She read those names and felt a mixture of relief and jealousy she had not expected. The harbor was becoming able to continue while she stopped being central to its unfinished sentences.

harbor_p23_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_056.text: On the evening before the public notice, Han asked Yue what she wanted her friends to remember. The traveler nearly answered with the project, then said she hoped they remembered she laughed at bad jokes and sometimes made worse ones. Han said this was an ambitious standard because the current archive already contained strong evidence of both. They laughed over privately bought tea. The clerk promised no public memorial to a visitor's virtues. Yue thanked her.

harbor_p23_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_057.text: Yue received four for the week's two half-days and six paid bed and meals. Twenty-six half-days had now been paid in the new term. Approved field costs were twelve ferries, six interpretation and four copies. Spending reached one hundred seventy-four, leaving twenty-six: wages four, bed six, ferries six, copies four, interpretation six. The separate emergency reserve remained one hundred seventy-two spent and sixty-eight unspent, with four unused stones. The maintenance council had reserved one new sixty-four, still unspent. Yue checked each source at its keeper and closed her personal note before supper.

harbor_p23_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_058.text: At dusk Lu Lian's permitted reply route produced a status that her inland son had received the message. It disclosed no address beyond the permissions given. Rong sent the actual confirmation through the ordinary return arrangement, and Han put it with the receiving question rather than the public index. Yue learned the limited result at work. She thought of the fish seller calling qi a poor trade for interesting light and smiled. The woman had needed a reader, a correct name and a reply. Those ordinary things could be worth a trip without making the coast a solved place.

harbor_p23_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p23_059.text: The twenty-fifth week's evening brought rain soft enough to make every patched roof sound different. Han and Yue sat beside the window listening without checking a public forecast every minute. The pilot's approval lay at its keeper; their table held bread, two cups and Han's unfinished painting board. Yue said her last paid week would begin tomorrow. The clerk nodded and asked whether she wanted the bread toasted. They spoke of the coming work once, then allowed the meal its own subject. Outside, three plans waited for one choice while the harbor continued doing things none of them had designed.
